clever adjective

also smart, bright (of a child), brilliant (very clever), she is smart, bright (smart), skilled, cleverness, skilfulness, bright (of a person), expressive (of the eyes), shrewdness, gifted, ingenious

classical

Wiktionary

Other words

  • ingeniōsus

    also used · classical · Traupman 158; Traupman 108: ingeniōsa est; Traupman 321 · Wiktionary

  • calliditās, calliditātis f. — cleverness, shrewdness, skill

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Nep. Eum. 1.3 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150, 158; Traupman 292 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • argūtus, argūta, argūtum — sharp, bright (of a person); expressive (of the eyes)

    also used · classical · Traupman 150, 152 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • artificiōsus, artificiōsa, artificiōsum — ingenious, skilful, artful

    also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 1.35 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 333 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Perhaps only in Cicero and the Rhetorica ad Herennium (Lewis & Short).

  • lūculentus, lūculenta, lūculentum — bright, full of light; splendid, excellent

    avoid · classical · Traupman 28, for “bright (smart)” · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short give “full of light, bright” and, of people, “excellent, distinguished”, not quick of mind. For a bright child, ingeniōsus or acūtus.

Examples

  • Ingeniōsa est.

    She is smart.Traupman 381
